Brief: Describe the Great Barrier Reef and the threats it faces.

1. The reef is located in the Coral Sea, off the coast of Queensland, Australia.
2. It is separated from the coast by a channel 160 kilometres (100 mi) wide in places and over 61 metres (200 ft) deep.
3. The Great Barrier Reef can be seen from outer space and is the world's biggest single structure made by living organisms.
4. This reef structure is composed of and built by billions of tiny organisms, known as coral polyps.
5. It supports a wide diversity of life and was selected as a World Heritage Site in 1981.
6. CNN labelled it one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World in 1997.
7. Australian World Heritage places included it in its list in 2007.
8. The Queensland National Trust named it a state icon of Queensland in 2006.
9. A large part of the reef is protected by the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park, which helps to limit the impact of human use, such as fishing and tourism.
10. The Great Barrier Reef has long been known to and used by the Aboriginal Australian and Torres Strait Islander peoples, and is an important part of local groups' cultures and spirituality.
11. The reef is a very popular destination for tourists, especially in the Whitsunday Islands and Cairns regions.
12. Tourism is an important economic activity for the region, generating over AUD$3 billion per year.
